clue.text: Hydro-electric schemes were a cult of the Sixties!

definitions.meaning: read whimsically as energy from a 'flower', crossword slang for a river, since it flows
the hippie movement preaching peace and love, its emblem a flower

explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords a 'flower' is often something that flows, a river; hydro-electric schemes run on river energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: river energy, playfully named, and the hippie peace-and-love slogan of the late 1960s.

clue.text: Admitted student to leading public school

parts.note: L is the learner plate abbreviation for a student driver
Eton College is England's best-known fee-paying school

explanation.surface: A pupil gains a place at a top private school.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'public school' is an old fee-charging private school; Eton is the most famous.
explanation.definitionFit: To let on is to reveal or confess, so admitted is a close synonym in the sense of owned up.

clue.text: Wish to grow old in Oxfordshire

parts.note: to wish for something is to want it
to age is to grow old

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to spend their retirement in the English countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the location: WANTAGE is a market town in Oxfordshire, a county west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Wantage is a market town in that southern English county, so 'in Oxfordshire' points to a place there.

clue.text: Withdraw declamatory words about the Common Market

indicators.note: about here means going around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a rant is a loud, declamatory speech
EC, the European Community, successor name of the Common Market

explanation.surface: A politician takes back a fiery speech about Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Common Market' was the popular British name for the European Economic Community, abbreviated EC.
explanation.definitionFit: To recant is to retract a stated belief, a synonym of withdraw in the sense of taking back words.

clue.text: Rota gent produced within the deadline

indicators.note: produced suggests the letters of the two words are made into something new

explanation.surface: A duty roster drawn up in time by a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced' rearranges ROTA and GENT into the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on target means on schedule, keeping to the planned time.

clue.text: Get out a further unit of gold

parts.note: further means additional, extra
ct is the abbreviation for carat, the measure of gold purity

explanation.surface: Someone retrieves yet another measure of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract is to draw or pull something out, a synonym of remove.

clue.text: Crooked Lancashire PC framed key police department

indicators.note: framed means set inside, as a picture in a frame
crooked means bent or twisted, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: B is one of the musical keys

explanation.surface: A bent Lancashire constable sets up a scapegoat for an important police unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crooked' jumbles LANCASHIRE and PC; 'framed' puts B (a key in music) among those letters. A PC is a police constable.
explanation.definitionFit: Special Branch is the British police unit handling national security and political crime.

clue.text: Wound dressing around crippled bone tissue

indicators.note: around means one piece wraps about the other

parts.note: lint is a soft fabric used to dress wounds
game is an old word for lame, as in a game leg

explanation.surface: A dressing is wrapped round an injured limb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' is the noun injury, not twisted. GAME as lame is old-fashioned ('a game leg').
explanation.definitionFit: A ligament is the tough fibrous band joining bone to bone at a joint.

clue.text: Undertook to sign

definitions.meaning: took on a task, committed oneself to doing it
to write one's name on a document

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means both to begin work on a task and literally to add a signature to a paper.

clue.text: Don is given a spell of bowling

definitions.meaning: to don clothes is to dress in them
in cricket a captain brings a bowler into the attack for a spell

explanation.surface: A university lecturer gets a turn bowling at cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like a university teacher but is the verb to wear. In cricket, a captain 'puts on' a bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses of the phrasal verb: to dress in clothes, and to bring a bowler into action in cricket.

clue.text: Allowed little time to dice

definitions.meaning: to chop food into small cubes

explanation.surface: A cook rushes the chopping.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to leave a tight margin, and read literally it means chopping something small.

clue.text: Ancient or otherwise carries the goods

definitions.note: a phrase describing a thing that holds cargo, standing for a noun

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Old or not, the vessel still delivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A container is a large box in which freight is shipped, so it holds cargo.

clue.text: Where Texans were massacred by an Alabama doctor

parts.note: MO is a Medical Officer, an army doctor

explanation.surface: A grim history of slaughter in Texas, with a Southern medic to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: The Alamo was the San Antonio mission where Texan defenders were killed by the Mexican army in 1836.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo is the mission fort in San Antonio where the Texan garrison was wiped out in 1836.

clue.text: Permitted to join a service band

parts.note: an arm is a branch of the armed services
let means allowed

explanation.surface: Someone is allowed to enlist in the forces band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' looks musical but is a strip worn round the upper arm.
explanation.definitionFit: An armlet is a ring or strip of material worn around the arm.

clue.text: Woman and man will be surrounded by rodents

indicators.note: surrounded by means one piece sits inside another

parts.note: mice are small rodents
he'll is a contraction of he will, a man in the future tense

explanation.surface: A woman and a man end up in a room full of mice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man will' is HE'LL, he will; the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Michelle is a common female first name.

clue.text: He enters estate management because he loves beauty

indicators.note: enters means one piece goes inside another
management suggests the letters are handled and reorganised

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man joins an estate agency because he appreciates beautiful things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'management' rearranges ESTATE to AESTTE; 'enters' puts HE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An aesthete is a person devoted to art and the appreciation of beauty.

clue.text: Wearing loose dresses at intervals during work

definitions.meaning: a shift is a simple loose dress, so this is dressed in such garments
staff working in turns or relays across the day

explanation.definitionFit: A shift is both a loose straight dress and a period of work taken in rotation.

clue.text: Getting commander into living accommodation

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: being means existing, living
Com. is an abbreviation of commander

explanation.surface: A naval officer is found somewhere to live.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming means growing or turning into, as getting does in 'getting cold'.

clue.text: He mustn't rub anyone up the wrong way

definitions.text: He mustn't rub anyone up the wrong way

parts.words: He mustn't rub anyone up the wrong way
parts.note: the idiom for annoying someone, read literally as a warning to a man who rubs people for a living

explanation.definitionFit: A massage therapist works by rubbing clients, so must do it soothingly.

clue.text: Grab a lot of eggs

definitions.meaning: a batch of eggs laid at one time

explanation.definitionFit: To clutch is to grasp hold of; a clutch is also a nest's batch of eggs.

clue.text: Garment gymnasts are told to change into?

definitions.text: Garment gymnasts are told to change into?

indicators.note: to change means the letters are switched into a new order

explanation.surface: Athletes are instructed what to put on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges ARE TOLD; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A leotard is the close-fitting one-piece garment worn by gymnasts and dancers.

clue.text: The Chancellor is a singer in church

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside another

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
the lark is a songbird

explanation.surface: A government minister sings in a church choir.
explanation.walkthrough: Kenneth Clarke was Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer, the finance minister, from 1993 to 1997.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenneth Clarke held the post of Chancellor of the Exchequer, Britain's finance minister, in the 1990s.

clue.text: Assists in finding Lincoln backstreet

parts.note: Abe was the familiar name of US president Abraham Lincoln

indicators.note: back means the following word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone helps by locating a side road in Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backstreet' splits as back + street: the abbreviation ST is turned round to TS.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to help or encourage, usually in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Greeting with very little point at the end of October

parts.note: hallo is a greeting
wee means very small
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A tiny welcome given at a month's close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' is a compass point, N for north.
explanation.definitionFit: Halloween falls on 31 October, the last day of the month.

clue.text: Joint where the Spanish acknowledge applause

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
a performer bows to acknowledge applause

explanation.surface: A Spanish audience cheers and a performer bows.
explanation.definitionFit: The elbow is the hinge joint between the upper arm and forearm.

clue.text: Demanded to be picked up at home

definitions.meaning: collected from one's house by someone visiting

explanation.definitionFit: Called for means both required, as a situation demands, and fetched from a house.

clue.text: A minute section of the circumference

parts.note: a bit is a piece or section

explanation.surface: A geometry lesson about part of a circle's edge.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambit is the bounds or limits surrounding something, its circuit or compass.

clue.text: Ticked off for not getting togged up

definitions.meaning: wearing casual clothes rather than smart ones

explanation.surface: Someone is reprimanded for turning up in casual clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressed down means both scolded severely and dressed informally, the opposite of dressing up.
